summary: Phase 2 celebration confetti feature verified end-to-end as Office Admin (blr1@finflow.com). All four required scenarios pass: (1) ROUTINE lead CREATE shows plain green folder-check overlay with caption 'Added successfully!' and NO celebration-confetti element; (2) MILESTONE lead CONVERT (POST /api/leads/{id}/convert → 201) shows confetti overlay with title 'Lead converted!' + subtitle 'A new student has been enrolled.', data-milestone='1', 70 confetti pieces, auto-dismisses in ~2.8s; (3) MILESTONE payment (POST /api/students/{id}/payments → 200) shows confetti overlay with title 'Payment recorded!' + subtitle 'The fee payment has been saved.', 70 confetti pieces, data-milestone='1'; (4) Overlay is non-blocking — computed pointer-events on both .celebrate-backdrop and .celebrate-card is 'none', and the underlying Convert dialog / Student page remained interactive during the celebration. No duplicate sonner toasts observed. Overlay disappears cleanly after the ~2.8s TTL.

critical_code_review_comments: milestoneFor() regex /\/convert$/ and /\/payments$/ correctly excludes GETs (method guard on line 19); good defensive design.
Confetti pieces count (70) is hard-coded in CelebrationOverlay.jsx — fine, but consider CONFETTI_COUNT constant next to CONFETTI_COLORS for parity/readability.
Confetti seed uses state.id (Date.now() + random) — stable across the overlay's lifetime, so pieces don't re-randomize on re-render. Good.
CelebrationOverlay renders confetti before card in JSX with pointer-events:none — no risk of blocking. Verified computed style at runtime.
